National Assembly
Session
2081 Ashad 12, Friday
Meeting Number - 20
The National Assembly meeting today commenced at 13:22 hrs under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members, the proceedings of today's National Assembly meeting (13:22 hrs) commence. Honourable members, names have been received to speak during the Zero Hour. I have allocated 1 minute each for speaking during the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Krishna Bahadur Rokaya.

Honourable Mr. Krishna Bahadur Rokaya (Nepali Congress):- (13:22 hrs)
Respected Chairperson, it is unfortunate that the reconstruction work for the earthquake-affected families of Jajarkot and Rukum Paschim has not yet begun, even though it has been over two and a half years since the earthquake centered in Jajarkot and Ramidanda on Kartik 17, 2080 BS. An estimated budget of 22 billion rupees is required for the reconstruction of the western earthquake, and 2.7 billion rupees are currently available in the Disaster Management Fund. Although the Honourable Finance Minister has stated in the presented budget that resources for earthquake reconstruction have been managed, the amount of budget is not visible anywhere. In Rukum Paschim alone, approximately 19,000 beneficiaries have been identified after the DDP. Although recommendations have been received from the local level for the identified beneficiaries, the process of requesting funds has not moved forward from the District Administration Office due to incomplete procedures, and the verification of re-submitted details is underway. Respected Chairperson, I strongly urge the Nepal Government, through your good self, to expedite the earthquake reconstruction work in Jajarkot and Rukum Paschim. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Ghanashyam Rizal.

Honourable Mr. Ghanashyam Rizal (Communist Party of Nepal):- Respected Chairperson, (13:23 hrs)
Following a significant increase in fuel prices citing the rise in international market prices, general consumers are facing steep price hikes in essential medicines, public transportation, daily consumer goods, and all other sectors. This has made the daily lives of ordinary citizens difficult. Businesses responsible for infrastructure construction have also fallen into trouble due to the increased cost of construction materials caused by the fuel price hike, leading to disruptions in the construction sector and the loss of employment for thousands of labourers. For some weeks, fuel prices have been falling significantly in the international market. It is an injustice to Nepali consumers to not reduce prices, citing various excuses, even when the purchase price is low. Therefore, I strongly draw the attention of the Nepal Government, through your good self, to immediately reduce fuel prices, control the rampant price hikes, and ease the daily lives of the general public. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar.

Honourable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress):- Respected Chairperson, (13:24 hrs)
While visually impaired persons and other persons with disabilities have been earning a livelihood through their skills, art, performances, and musical presentations in various cities across Nepal, including the Kathmandu Valley, the current government arrested them from the Tilganga area on Jestha 7, prevented them from working, and kept them in a holding centre. On the pretext of not allowing them to work there, these visually impaired friends have been staging a continuous protest at Maitighar since Ashad 7, but the government has not listened to them yet. Therefore, I strongly demand that the government bring a program for the immediate resettlement of these visually impaired friends and that the government does not create any obstacles for them to perform their musical programs and work for their livelihood. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Renu Chand.

Honourable Ms. Renu Chand (Communist Party of Nepal):- Respected Chairperson, (13:24 hrs)
It was right to impose a fine of 3 lakh rupees when a cockroach was found in the omelette the minister was about to eat. How much fine should be imposed on the government when insects are found in the food of the landless, or will the government manage the landless only after reaching the position of power? Evicting them, is this what is meant by 'filtering those who know'? Currently, the government is evicting the landless from the holding centres. They claim to have magical abilities to solve every problem, yet they are violating the human rights of the landless. This government lacks ideological clarity, conceptual clarity, makes irresponsible comments about borders, tries to play with federalism, and the Prime Minister is busy joking on Facebook. I am concerned about where this misguided government will lead the country. The government cannot remove the landless without proper management. 

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota.

Honourable Ms. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress):- Respected Chairperson, (13:26 hrs)
Is the order to vacate the holding centres with a resettlement amount of 24,000 rupees as relief a just and complete decision? It is not easy to find a place to rent in Kathmandu, and moreover, it is very difficult with the current inflation. Being born poor is not the fault of a citizen, government. It was a play of fate. According to the Constitution of Nepal, is it not the government's responsibility to manage food, shelter, clothing, education, and health, which fall under the "fundamental rights" of Nepali citizens to have the right to live? Today, the government is treating the landless inhumanely. Those who were bulldozed from their safe places without prior preparation and brought to the streets, kept in holding centres with the hope of permanent settlement, and then evicted from there without management, where will they go now? Is it appropriate for the government to act so irresponsibly? Are the landless not Nepali citizens? The government must provide a safe place and a sustainable solution for the identification of genuine landless, problem-solving, employment, and sustainable management of shelter, as per the government's own statement, as soon as possible, by exercising constitutional rights, otherwise, such behaviour will lead the country, government, and (...time expired).

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Bishnu Devi Pudasaini.

Honourable Ms. Bishnu Devi Pudasaini (Nepali Congress):- Respected Chairperson, (13:28 hrs)
I believe that imposing a 3% tax on education and health in the tax proposal presented by the Honourable Finance Minister is extremely inhumane. I urge that this proposal be withdrawn. Furthermore, I welcome the decision to include Gokarna Forest in the World Heritage List. I also request the government, through the Honourable House, to operate the Bagmati corridor from Sundarijal to Guhyeshwori by relocating approximately 300 meters of land belonging to the Gokarna Resort before it is included in the World Heritage List. This will also help reduce traffic congestion in Gokarna, Jorpati, and Chabahil. I conclude by wishing you farewell. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma.

Honourable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Communist Party of Nepal):- Respected Chairperson, (13:29 hrs)
The current government, established with the slogan of good governance, has bulldozed and evicted thousands of landless people and is keeping them in holding centres. Then, they are being evicted from the holding centres, and it is unknown where they are being taken. The landless are being evicted with 25,000 rupees in their pockets. This is a blatant violation of the Constitution of Nepal, a violation of human rights, and a violation of the right to housing guaranteed by the Constitution of Nepal. The government's attempt to remove the landless without permanent management is inappropriate. Therefore, the landless should be fully managed, permanently managed, and only then should they be moved from the holding centres. I wish to draw the serious attention of the Nepal Government to this. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Shreekrishna Prasad Adhikari.

Honourable Mr. Shreekrishna Prasad Adhikari (Communist Party of Nepal):- Respected Chairperson, (13:30 hrs)
The government, through the empowered Bagmati Civilization Integrated Development Committee, has issued a notice for landless people residing in the holding centre to vacate the camp within five days, providing them 24,000 rupees. The government, which has already made a serious mistake by evicting the settlements of landless and unmanaged residents without proper alternative housing arrangements, is now making another serious mistake by evicting landless people from the camp without arranging permanent housing, breaking its promise to provide land ownership certificates within 60 days. Respected Chairperson, I want to warn the government: do not immediately stop the act of evicting landless children, the infirm, the sick, the helpless, and the poor from the camps and leaving them stranded on the streets during this rainy season without permanent arrangements for housing and employment. Thank you, greetings.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Savitri Malla.

Honourable Ms. Savitri Malla (Communist Party of Nepal):- Respected Chairperson, (13:31 hrs)
This government, which is dancing and singing in Chitwan, is forcibly evicting people, with 93% women in the holding centres, 44% chronically ill, unable to afford medicine. The government is forcibly evicting landless and unmanaged residents who have been living in various risky settlements along riverbanks in the Kathmandu Valley and other parts of the country for decades, without considering basic needs like food, shelter, education, health, and employment. They were kept in various holding centres with the promise of temporary management and permanent solutions within 60 days, but their management has not happened anywhere, anytime, or how. I heard that a notice was posted to vacate the holding centre by 12 PM today, taking 24,000 rupees as management expenses (.. time expired).

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members, the order of speaking during the Zero Hour concludes here. (13:32 hrs)
Honourable members, names have been received on a party basis to speak during the Special Time. I will now provide time to the Honourable members to speak. First, Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar, time 12 minutes. Following this, Honourable Member Urmila Aryal.

Honourable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress):- Respected Chairperson, (13:33 hrs)
Today, I wish to express some of my personal and party views on a few current issues in the House. Respected Chairperson, for the past week, it has seemed as if there is no government in Kathmandu. Kathmandu is the capital of the country, but it appears as if the country's capital has shifted to Chitwan. No representative of the government has been found in Kathmandu, and its direct impact has been observed in Parliament and in many other government activities. While the government remained busy with its activities in Chitwan, I went to Maitighar Mandala to meet some Nepali brothers and sisters who were dissatisfied with the government's activities, felt wronged, and were denied their rights.

Respected Chairperson, at Maitighar Mandala, on one hand, students, including many from Class 12, are protesting due to the injustice caused by the government's mistakes in publishing the Class 12 examination results. I am surprised, I do not know which front of the Gen Z movement the ministers of this government were on, but the Gen Z movement...

Those brothers and sisters of grade 11-12 who were walking in front on every front were wronged by the government formed on the basis of that Gen Z movement. In the name of publishing exam results quickly and showing quick work, the Ministry of Education made a mistake, and our young brothers and sisters of that Gen Z movement became victims of that mistake, and they were seen protesting and demonstrating at Maitighar Mandala demanding justice. Not only that, Honorable Chairperson, the government, in the name of cleaning up Kathmandu city, in the name of making this Kathmandu city beautiful and pleasant, in the name of making this Kathmandu city civilized, the government has committed an act against poor, helpless, and disabled individuals, which is extremely condemnable. This cannot be tolerated. More than 1 million disabled people have been watching this closely, and the entire disabled community has been condemning this misconduct of the government and the police administration. However, the government has not even once talked to those individuals or discussed their demands, even though the protest has been going on for the 8th day today. Not only that, Honorable Chairperson, the people of the Vadi community are protesting, saying their self-respect has been hurt. Not only that, some Dalit rights activists are protesting, demanding "Does the government have a room?" Not only that, professional organizations including papad makers are protesting, demanding their right to express their views and to earn a living through their profession. However, the protesting friends have stated that the government is pretending not to hear the voices and issues of the people. I want to ask the government, the government, you are in power with a huge majority, with the votes of those citizens who protested, promising to give "good governance" to those citizens, to give "justice" to those citizens, to "govern the state through the rule of law" to those citizens, and you are in government today. But even before 90 days of your coming to power, before the honeymoon period of the Balen government is over, before 100 days are over, the disillusionment that has arisen among the citizens today, the citizens are increasingly protesting, which is very sad. As a Nepali citizen, even though I am a Member of Parliament from the opposition party, I want this government to do good work. I want this government to complete its full five-year term. I want this government to protect the democracy and republic of our country, provide the rule of law, and fulfill the development expectations of the Nepali people. However, the growing disillusionment among the citizens towards the government is showing a very bad omen, and I want to alert the government about this. However, without considering all these things, without considering these everyday matters, the government is moving forward with its own attitude. Just yesterday, the government has started a jihad from Chitwan. The government, Rastriya Swatantra Party, has said that the provincial assemblies of this country should be abolished when our time comes, and the National Assembly should be restructured. The government and the ruling party, Rastriya Swatantra Party, have passed this. I want to ask the government, does the Balen government have no other business to do? The government, the price hike of petroleum products, after the great war between America and Iran, there has been a huge price hike, and in the context of adjusting the price of that commodity, the Nepali people are using petroleum products by paying exorbitant prices. Can't the government work to adjust the price of petroleum products? Or will it just talk about federalism? Another question I have for the government is that more than 12 kharba rupees are currently piled up in banks. Small and medium-sized entrepreneurs are unable to get loans from banks and are struggling to promote their businesses. With such national and international expertise, when the Finance Minister is in place, shouldn't the government work on how to channel that money and bring it into Nepal's economy? But the government is not paying attention to that. The health insurance program is almost in a coma. Citizens are wondering whether to go to the hospital for treatment or not. The government is unable to allocate budget for that program and work towards its continuation. Not only that, the government has not uttered a word about the investigation it promised to conduct through a commission regarding the involvement of the security bodies after August 23 and 24. However, the government is scattered everywhere, stirring up issues of garbage and water, and stirring up political issues that have already been settled, which is a very serious matter. I want to tell the government, "Government, please don't put your nose everywhere untimely. You have many tasks to do regarding good governance, development, and corruption control. I request the government to focus on those." Finally, the Rastriya Swatantra Party, the current ruling party, held its Chitwan convention. According to the party's own workers, the performance was weak. If the government's performance in governing is also weak, then the Nepali people will not forgive not only the Rastriya Swatantra Party but also many other parties. Borrowing the words of former Prime Minister Dr. Baburam Bhattarai, I would like to conclude my remarks by saying, "Government, please focus on the foundation on which you were born, the issues you were born with. The government was born for development, the government was born to promote good governance, the government was born to control corruption. Focus on that, and do not meddle in settled political issues like identity politics without reason." I would like to conclude my remarks by giving this suggestion to the government. Thank you, Namaste. Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Urmila Aryal, time 11 minutes. (13:44) After this, Honorable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri. Honorable Ms. Urmila Aryal (Communist Party of Nepal): Honorable Chairperson (13:44) Sir, now with new elections and a new government formed, I want to express my views in the hope that a government formed with a large mandate will start working by adopting some new approaches. And first of all, I am a resident of Birgunj. I was also born in Parsa district, and I want to say something regarding the proposal from Russia and special discussion on the National Sugar Policy concerning the operation of Birgunj Sugar Factory. My father also worked in a sugar mill for a few days. Therefore, I have immense respect for that sugar mill, and especially for all the people of the Madhesh, the relationship is quite good. Now, with that sugar mill closed and in a state of collapse, we are all worried, aren't we? Therefore, at the present time, while discussing this, considering the demand for sugar, the supply of sugar, and the current situation, the construction of national income and employment, Birgunj Sugar Factory, Lumbini Sugar Factory, etc., are all important, but I am talking about the current situation. I had written other things too, but I felt like shortening it and took only one. Chairperson Sir, I have come to know from various recent news about sugar and public enterprises, the government's program to re-operate seven public enterprises, and discussions held between the Russian Ambassador and the Vice President of Nepal regarding Birgunj Sugar Factory and Janakpur Cigarette Factory, and I believe the National Assembly has also been drawn to this proposal. I will primarily focus more on the sugar factory in this regard. We always have a shortage of sugar. It is well known that sugar is an essential food item for domestic use, industrial production, and the service sector, and I don't think I need to elaborate. According to various estimates, the total current demand for sugar is 270,000 metric tons, of which 175,000 metric tons are for domestic consumption and 94,000 metric tons are for industry and service sectors. The demand for sugar is projected to grow at an annual rate of 5 percent in the future. Thus, in the next decade, the total demand for sugar will be 440,000 metric tons. In fact, as Nepal's total population increases from 30 million to 40 million and per capita income increases from US$1500 to US$5000, the total demand for sugar will further increase, and thus it is essential to protect sugar. This is inevitable. I had prepared the supply of sugar in a point-wise manner. Currently, the supply of sugar is much lower than its demand, and Nepal has been facing risks of sugar shortage and price manipulation. Even the available goods are hidden, sold at high prices, and black marketing occurs. According to current data, sugar production in the country has decreased to about 120,000 metric tons, and Nepal needs to import about 150,000 metric tons of sugar to meet the deficit. The public debate about increasing supply through national sugar production is ironic. Instead of increasing our own production, we are becoming import-dependent. Nepal has traditionally imported sugar from countries like India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, etc. However, India has recently moved sugar from the list of controlled items to prohibited items, and there will be a severe shortage of sugar. There are opportunities for businesses in Nepal to balance the sugar market dynamically. However, mismanagement and policy ad-hocism must be overcome. We have not been able to do that. For example, if farmers receive a good price for sugarcane, sugarcane production and supply can be increased quickly. According to various studies, if the price of sugarcane increases by 1 percent, sugarcane production increases by 0.4 to 0.7 percentage points. It is necessary to make proper use of this relationship between sugarcane supply and market price. The capacity utilization rate of about a dozen sugar mills currently in operation is about 44

It is only 48 percent. There are ample grounds to increase this, aren't there? The sugar recovery rate from sugarcane in sugar mills in Nepal is 8 to 9 percent, whereas there is potential to increase this to the world average of 12 to 14 percent. Based on Nepal's natural resources such as land, climate, water resources, irrigation, energy, botanical genetics, and human labor, for national income, capital formation, and employment, the country can not only become self-reliant in sugar but also has strong potential to export its produced sugar to various countries. For example, Nepal can export sugar to Tibet in China, Afghanistan, and Central Asian countries. Nepal had, has, and will have a comparative and competitive position. In the context mentioned above, some socialist countries have also helped Nepal's industrial development by establishing sugar mills. For example, the former Soviet Union built the Birgunj Sugar Factory, and the Chinese government built the Lumbini Sugar Factory as gifts to the Nepali people. However, due to the neo-liberal, flawed socio-economic philosophy and practices of some stakeholders and governments in Nepal, these industries have collapsed, which is a bitter reality before us, and the entire sugarcane and sugar industry is in an underdeveloped state. This needs to change. Currently, there is a capital investment of approximately NRs 24 to 30 billion in the sugar industry. The sugar production capacity is approximately 350,000 to 400,000 metric tons per year. The combined contribution of sugarcane and sugar to the total GDP is about 1 percent, and about 100,000 farming families are involved in sugarcane cultivation, and about 34,000 people are employed in sugar mills, with many more employed in related service sectors. Therefore, if the value addition chain of sugarcane and sugar can be developed, the above achievements can be doubled. Birgunj Sugar Factory, now that I am a resident of Birgunj, I want to focus on the Birgunj Sugar Factory itself. The Birgunj Sugar Factory is a national heritage established by the United Nations in 1964. However, primarily due to the aforementioned policy flaws, that facility is currently closed. There is a shortage of sugar in the country. The assets of the Birgunj Sugar Factory are as follows: Factory compound 64 bigha, Industrial wastewater treatment compound 16 bigha, Sugarcane farm in Simra 790 bigha, and countless other sugarcane areas in Bara, Parsa, Rautahat. The only sugarcane development farm of the National Agricultural Research Council (NARC) associated with Birgunj Sugar Factory is also located there in Jitpur. It is well known that Birgunj Sugar Factory has been closed, and its assets related to sugarcane development and sugar mills have been misappropriated, misused, and encroached upon. Also, Nepal has failed to appreciate the contribution made by friendly countries. Furthermore, the sugarcane research and development programs of NARC are also in a dilapidated state. Regarding the re-operation of Birgunj Sugar Factory and its modality. The utilization, conservation, and development of the assets of Birgunj Sugar Factory can address a great need of the nation. In fact, this factory should be made a multipurpose factory with a capacity of 4,000 TCD instead of the previous 14,000 TCD (tons per day) capacity from 52 years ago. The benefits of doing so will be as follows: It will be the largest bio-processing factory in South Asia, Sugarcane processing will be 600,000 tons, Bio-ethanol distillery will be 50,000 liters per day, Electricity generation will be 25 megawatts, which it can supply, and NEA can also buy it, Organic fertilizer production will be 24,000 tons. Capital investment for developing Birgunj Sugar Factory will be approximately NRs 4.5 to 6.5 billion. Employment generation will be approximately 35,000 jobs. Permanent jobs will be 650, temporary jobs 600, sugarcane production 30,000, transportation etc. 3,500, net profit will be 16 to 19 percent. The investment cost ratio will be 2.25 to 2.40 Benefit Cost Ratio. The return Internal Rate of Return will be 24.1 to 26.8 percent. Conclusion and Suggestions: The government should promptly formulate a sugarcane and sugar policy. The facilities, assets, and development plans provided by Russia, China, and other friendly countries in the sugar sector should be made public. The programs of the National Agricultural Research Council (NARC) for sugarcane research and development should be promptly addressed. The capacity, technology, management, and sustainability of sugar mills should be modified. Sugar industries should be linked to electricity generation, alternative energy, potable alcohol, and organic fertilizer production in addition to sugar production. It is seen that self-reliance in sugar should be achieved and an export-oriented promotion should be built. The sugar industry chain should be operated on 3Ps, most importantly, Public-Private Partnership. The above policies and industries are policy-driven, sorry, I made it a bit long, thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri, time 10 minutes. (13:56 hrs) After this, Honorable Member Puja Chaudhary. Honorable Ms. Ram Kumari Jhankri (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honorable Chairperson, this repeated and ongoing process of spasms is happening. Therefore, it seems necessary to weigh what to say and what not to say. When the country was devastated by the earthquake. When Nepal's pride and hope were lost. At that time, a foreign Portuguese player, Cristiano Ronaldo, raised the Nepali flag on a jersey with 'Nepal' written on it at the Real Madrid ground. At that time, all Nepalis felt a sense of pride, that someone stood with us, loved us, showed solidarity, and said 'we are with you', giving confidence and applying balm to the wounds of broken hearts. At that very time, the 'Occupy Baluwatar' movement was ongoing in Nepal, wrapped in the national flag. Where had that 'Occupy Baluwatar' movement reached? When there was a blockade, we were coming out of it, and after that, there was the COVID-19 pandemic. During that pandemic, the 'Occupy Baluwatar' movement was translated into the 'Enough is Enough' movement in America. These are the same people who, carrying the national flag on their shoulders, ran the 'Enough is Enough' movement, and these same people attempted to burn down the country on August 23 and 24, 2082. When Cristiano Ronaldo raised the Portuguese and Nepali flags, Nepalis felt pride. Some social media influencers, artists, and a few so-called social activists in Nepal, who carried the flag on their shoulders, burned down the country. They burned down the administrative center of Singha Durbar, burned data, burned facts, burned the heart of the judiciary, burned the office of the Head of State, and generally burned down the country, and this burning of the country was called a revolution. What kind of revolution was this? And an investigation commission was formed to investigate that revolution. I won't talk about that, but let's discuss the Human Rights Commission. The Human Rights Commission submitted its report late and recommended action by making retrospective laws, thereby targeting some political individuals. Therefore, I want to ask what is the jurisdiction of the Human Rights Commission? What is the scope of the Human Rights Commission? What should it investigate, what should it recommend? And it submits this report, and Article 20 of the Constitution of Nepal 2072, the right to criminal justice, is a fundamental right, which prohibits the state from committing atrocities against citizens through retrospective laws. Such a recommendation has been made. Nevertheless, there are some recommendations regarding the events of August 23 and 24, even if they are from some neighbors. But this government is turning a deaf ear to the people declared criminals in those recommendations and shows no initiative to take action. But I have a question about the jurisdiction of human rights. Can retrospective laws be made or not? And I would like to request the Human Rights Commission to read the Constitution of Nepal once. At that very time, after all this was burned down, this government was formed. This government gave the slogan of good governance and delivery. The slogan of good governance was so strong that its own party leader, who is facing criminal charges, did not want to obtain a certificate of innocence through a fair trial in court, claiming innocence. The government has taken the easy way out. Is this good governance? And at the same time, to silence the leaders of rival political parties, to practice democracy in the model of Bangladesh and Pakistan, people are being targeted, arrested, and silenced; businessmen are being arrested and silenced; civil society is being arrested and silenced. The current center of this is targeting former Prime Minister Comrade KP Sharma Oli, former Home Minister, and currently a leader of the CPN-UML, former Finance Minister, based on the statement of one person. If a major investigation is to be conducted based on a statement, and if the person is always available for questioning, should this be done or not? Therefore, this is an attempt to silence this voice. Therefore, I think we need to pay attention to this attempt to silence this voice. As for delivery, it is already visible. This is a government that runs on the express highway. The Prime Minister of this government has said, "We only need an accelerator, we don't need a brake." "We only need an accelerator, we don't need a brake." Therefore, this government, running on the express highway, does not seek medicine for cancer treatment, there is no rabies vaccine, there is no chemical fertilizer, there is no health insurance, there are no beds in hospitals, there is no control over bird flu, there is no management of squatters. These visually impaired friends who were earning a living by singing on the streets have been removed without alternative arrangements. It has reached a point where the Class 12 results were released on the express highway, and most students failed, and there is no way to provide satisfactory results for them. Therefore, if we understand that this is heading towards an accident, it is because going on this express highway is the only way. Where there is balance for any vehicle to run. But when the balance is lost, no matter how wide the road is, no matter how broad the road is, no matter how straight the road is, it will lead to nothing but an accident. And there is discussion about the much-talked-about visit of the ruling party leader to India and the visit of our Nepali government's Foreign Minister to India. I personally told Foreign Minister Honorable Shishir Khanal that at least one person in this government will have dialogue, so today I consider him good as a minister. But after his visit, 83 tea industries closed down, and exports stopped. Now, the Finance Minister of this government was saying that we have to implement the "More Productive" principle in Nepal, that we have to implement this "Productive" principle. That means, what is the "More Productive" principle for? It is to understand India's interests, to cooperate in mutual interests, not to work for the interests of another country by abandoning national interests. This is understood from this. Otherwise, after the much-discussed, anticipated, and successful visit to India, regarding issues from border disputes to exports, where is the government? Therefore, I want to ask a question and urge the government to pay attention to this matter.

I would like to request. Regarding the Human Rights Commission, I have already spoken about this commission, the jurisdiction of this commission needs to be discussed, and a judicial commission should be formed to investigate the incidents of August 23 and 24. Let the judicial commission be headed by a sitting judge of the Supreme Court. Let the commission investigate the incidents of August 22 and 23 in a planned manner, who directed and decided to run this movement, and who took action in the field and caused the country to burn today. These arsonists, traitors, and anti-nationals must be brought to justice by the judicial commission to be formed, and Nepal's self-respect must be upheld. We must not remain silent now. If we MPs remain silent, with tape on our mouths, in the ruins of this burning Singha Durbar, we will be making a big mistake for our future generations, leaving behind a great sin. Therefore, whether handcuffs are put on our hands, shackles on our feet, or nails hammered, we must all unite to identify and defeat those who have been working to disrupt our peace, security, and order through various movements by infiltrating this government and its processes, and those who have been systematically undermining the people's dream of development since 2072. It is time for the poor to rise up. Because this government has said that the poor are not our people, because this government belongs to the middle class, it only talks about the middle class and foreign agents. Therefore, the 20 percent of the people living below the poverty line and the 17.5 percent living below the multidimensional poverty line, you must speak up. We are here to speak for you in Parliament. We are your representatives in villages and settlements. We will not delay in raising your voice now because the honeymoon period of this government's 100 days is also over, and we will account for everything. We will hold accountable those who burn this country, conspire with foreign powers, and sell information from the cabinet. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Puja Chaudhary, time 5 minutes. After this (14:07 hrs) Honorable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma. Honorable Ms. Puja Chaudhary (Janasamajwadi Party, Nepal):- Honorable Chairperson, every year, paddy transplantation starts across the country from mid-Asar 15 and ends by Shrawan 14, which has become like the farmers' annual calendar. Last year, farmers in Madhesh Province faced drought problems during the transplantation season. As there was no water in the canals, it was not possible to transplant paddy in the dry fields on time. The question remains whether our leaders will gain wisdom regarding this. Local elections are approaching. Such a destructive situation is being created in the country. We are not hearing that discussions are being intensified where they should be focused soon. We are concerned. What can we do to regain our lost prestige from yesterday and bring it back on track? We all need to be concerned about this. I feel we should not hesitate to offer suggestions to our leadership. Similarly, there is a lot of discussion going on about the constitutional amendment debate paper. I have heard that many workshops and discussions have taken place. We are all aware of this subject, but what is the stance of our parties on constitutional amendment? The stance of the parties is our stance. We have heard the views of the leaders of the main opposition parties. They say that discussions can be held on issues other than federalism, democracy, and republicanism. We are ready to amend it, but our discussion will not be to weaken the constitution. This has a long background. We have also heard the views of the CPN-UML, and they have also said that discussions can be held without undermining the values and core spirit of the constitution, and that it can be further enriched. However, it is not known that the parties themselves have taken steps to initiate discussions. Discussions are necessary among all parties. Looking at it this way, the Nepali Congress and UML seem to be looking to discuss the situation more or less as it is, but I see slightly different issues from the CPN and Madhesi parties and other smaller parties. Why? Because the executive head of state, and full proportional representation, has been a long-standing issue of the CPN. There has been a reservation on this issue since yesterday. Rashtriya Swatantra Party has also raised this issue now. Madhesi parties are also not outside this issue. These are our general topics. However, RPP has raised many issues in their convention, which has made us serious. For example, making the National Assembly a council of experts, a council of 30 people, or abolishing it; making the Vice President the Chairperson of the National Assembly; abolishing the District Coordination Committee; reducing local levels; increasing wards; making only one ward chairperson, etc. Many such issues have been raised. We need to discuss these issues too, don't we? If we don't discuss whether this is right or wrong, and from what perspective it has come, then what happens is that we might suddenly move in a different direction. I end my speech here. Thank you. Honorable Speaker: Honorable members, the order of speaking during special time ends here. (14:03) Honorable members, a letter regarding the authentication of bills has been received from the Office of the President. I will now inform you of the contents of that letter. Subject: Regarding the authentication of bills. I request that a copy of the bill authenticated by the Honorable President Ram Chandra Paudel in accordance with Article 113, Sub-section 2 of the Constitution of Nepal, along with this letter, be sent. Bill Number: 03 Bill Name: Alternative Development Finance Mobilization Bill, 2083 Date of Authentication: 2083/03/11. Mahadev Panth, Secretary 2083 Ashad 19. Honorable members, I now provide time to the Secretary of the National Assembly, Mr. Tul Bahadur Kandel, to inform the assembly of the message received from the House of Representatives regarding the Appropriation Bill, 2083, and to table it. National Assembly Secretary Mr. Tul Bahadur Kandel: Honorable Speaker Sir, (14:04) A message regarding a bill passed by the House of Representatives has been received. With the permission of the Speaker, I will inform the assembly of the said message in accordance with the provisions of Rule 133 (A), Sub-rule 1 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075. Mr. Secretary, National Assembly. Subject: Bill sent with message. The "Appropriation Bill, 2083", which originated in the House of Representatives, was passed by the House of Representatives on Thursday, Ashad 4, 2083, without amendment. Therefore, in accordance with Rule 127, Sub-rule 1 of the House of Representatives Rules, 2083, the bill is sent with a message. Prakash Adhikari, Secretary 2083 Ashad 4. Honorable Speaker Sir, with the permission of the Speaker, in accordance with the provisions of Rule 133 (A), Sub-rule 1 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, I table the said message before this honorable assembly. Thank you. Honorable Speaker: Honorable members, I now present a motion of condolence on the demise of Mr. Rajendra Kharel, former member of the House of Representatives and former minister. (14:06) Born in Kharelthok, Kavrepalanchok district in 2003 BS, former member of the House of Representatives and former minister Rajendra Kharel passed away at the age of 80 on Ashad 7, 2083. This meeting of the National Assembly expresses deep sorrow over his demise. Mr. Kharel was elected as a member of the House of Representatives from Kavrepalanchok constituency number 4 in the general elections of 2056 BS from the Nepali Congress party. He also held the responsibilities of State Minister for Education and Minister for Women, Children, and Social Welfare. This meeting expresses heartfelt tribute to the late Mr. Kharel and deep condolences to the bereaved family. Honorable members, I request that the motion of condolence be passed. Honorable members, I declare the motion of condolence unanimously passed. Honorable members, let us now stand for one minute of silence to express sorrow over the demise of Mr. Rajendra Kharel, former member of the House of Representatives and former minister. (Moment of Silence) Thank you. The next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Monday, Ashad 15, 2083, at 12:15 PM. Honorable members, this meeting is adjourned until then. (Thereafter, this meeting was adjourned until Monday, Ashad 15, 2083, at 12:15 PM.) Adjourned: 15:09.

sections.summary_en: The meeting commenced at 13:22 hrs under the chairpersonship of Narayan Prasad Dahal. The Chairperson announced the commencement of the Zero Hour and allocated one minute per speaker.

sections.name: Zero Hour
sections.summary_en: Several members raised concerns during the Zero Hour. Krishna Bahadur Rokaya highlighted the delayed reconstruction efforts for earthquake victims in Jajarkot and Rukum Paschim. Ghanashyam Rizal spoke about the impact of rising fuel prices on consumers and businesses. Padam Bahadur Pariyar raised the issue of visually impaired artists being prevented from performing. Renu Chand criticized the government's handling of landless squatters and its overall lack of clarity. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota questioned the resettlement of landless people and the government's responsibility towards citizens' fundamental rights. Bishnu Devi Pudasaini opposed the proposed tax on education and health and welcomed the inclusion of Gokarna Forest in the World Heritage List. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma condemned the eviction of landless people without proper management. Shreekrishna Prasad Adhikari criticized the government's eviction of landless people from holding centres without alternative housing. Savitri Malla also spoke about the forced eviction of landless people and the inadequate management in holding centres.

sections.summary_en: The Chairperson announced the commencement of the Special Time and called upon Padam Bahadur Pariyar to speak, followed by Urmila Aryal. Padam Bahadur Pariyar expressed his views on current issues, noting the government's apparent absence from Kathmandu and the impact on parliamentary proceedings. He also mentioned meeting with citizens protesting at Maitighar Mandala.

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The speaker raises concerns about the government's actions affecting various groups, including students, visually impaired individuals, the Vadi community, Dalits, and professional organizations. They criticize the government's perceived inaction and lack of dialogue with protesting citizens.

speakers.topic: Government's inaction and citizen protests

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker criticizes the government's focus on settling political issues and diverting attention from crucial matters like petroleum price hikes, economic stagnation, and the failing health insurance program. They also mention the Rastriya Swatantra Party's proposal to abolish provincial assemblies and restructure the National Assembly.

speakers.name: Honorable Member Urmila Aryal
speakers.topic: Government's misplaced priorities and economic issues

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker transitions to discussing the Birgunj Sugar Factory and the National Sugar Policy, highlighting the importance of the sugar industry for national income and employment. They detail the current demand and projected future demand for sugar, emphasizing the need for increased domestic production and addressing import dependency.

speakers.name: Honorable Ms. Urmila Aryal
speakers.topic: Birgunj Sugar Factory and National Sugar Policy

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker further elaborates on the sugar supply situation, noting the deficit and the risks of price manipulation. They discuss the potential for increasing sugarcane production by offering better prices to farmers and the need to improve capacity utilization in existing sugar mills.

speakers.name: Honorable Ms. Urmila Aryal
speakers.topic: Sugar supply challenges and sugarcane farming

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker discusses the potential of Nepal's sugar industry, highlighting issues with current production rates and the need for modernization. They propose a plan to revive the Birgunj Sugar Factory into a multi-purpose facility with significant economic and employment benefits. The speaker also criticizes the government's approach to governance, delivery, and human rights, citing specific examples of policy failures and political targeting.

speakers.name: Ram Kumari Jhankri
speakers.topic: Sugarcane and sugar industry, Birgunj Sugar Factory revival, government's failures

key_issues: Political targeting and suppression of dissent

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: A member raised concerns about the Human Rights Commission and called for a judicial inquiry into recent incidents. Another member highlighted the plight of farmers in Madhesh Province due to malfunctioning irrigation systems and called for government attention. A third member spoke about the displacement of landless Dalits and squatters, questioning the government's actions and the lack of constitutional rights fulfillment. Finally, a member criticized the government's extradition treaty with India, arguing it benefits India more and compromises Nepal's sovereignty. They also raised issues concerning squatters' rights, the film 'Lali Bazaar', and the repression of artists.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker criticizes the ruling party for potentially undermining the constitution and federalism, drawing parallels to past political systems. Concerns are raised about the government's handling of various issues including border disputes, landless problems, and worker welfare in tea gardens. The speaker also touches upon the erosion of democratic norms and the importance of national sovereignty.

speakers.name: Rabi Lamichhane
speakers.topic: Criticism of ruling party, federalism, and constitutional integrity

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker expresses concern over the perceived weakening of the National Assembly and criticizes proposals to make it a body for experts rather than elected representatives. The speaker highlights issues like the landless problem, breakdown in communication between the President and PM, border disputes, and unresolved issues of trade unions and student unions.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker questions the removal of seniority distinctions and the disregard for the order of precedence, suggesting it reflects a broader erosion of constitutional values. The speaker warns that attempts to undermine the constitution could lead to severe political unrest and foreign interference.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker discusses the issue of unused ballot papers from past elections and calls for an investigation. Concerns are raised about the government's failure to present reports from various commissions, leading to a lack of resolution for pressing issues. The speaker warns of a severe political storm if the constitution is undermined.

speakers.name: Khimbahadur Khatri
speakers.topic: Commissions and reports

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker emphasizes that the upcoming movement will be devastating due to threats to national independence and potential foreign interference. The speaker urges seriousness, highlighting the National Assembly's role in policy-making and warning against aggressive nationalism. The speaker also advises ministers that governments are temporary and should focus on serving the people.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker criticizes the current government for failing to uphold democratic culture and values, citing the lack of dialogue between the President and PM. The speaker stresses the accountability of the elected Prime Minister to the parliament and warns of further protests if this accountability is not met.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Goma Devi Timalsina raises the issue of closed tea industries in Ilam and Jhapa and the plight of affected workers, urging the government to facilitate an agreement. She expresses confidence that the minister, being independently elected, will convey their concerns to the Prime Minister.

speakers.name: Goma Devi Timalsina
speakers.topic: Tea industry workers' plight and government action

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Members of the National Assembly raised concerns about various issues including the plight of displaced people, infrastructure development in Hetauda, the operation of industries, and the government's approach to good governance. They criticized the government for failing to address the needs of the people and demanded accountability.

speakers.name: Rukmini Koirala
speakers.topic: Squatters' rights, inflation, fertilizer shortage, bird flu, petroleum prices, paddy transplantation

speakers.name: Basudev Ghimire
speakers.topic: Earthquake condolences, squatters' rights, drought, fertilizer shortage, federalism, health services, provincial hospitals, airports

sections.name: Special Time
sections.summary_en: Honorable member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar spoke on contemporary issues including road safety, foreign employment, political party dynamics, and constitutional amendment debates. He urged the government to address road accidents and the negative impacts of foreign employment, and called for unity among political parties to strengthen the nation. He also highlighted the need for broad discussions on constitutional amendments.

speakers.name: Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar
speakers.topic: Contemporary issues: roads, foreign employment, politics, constitution

sections.name: Other Business
sections.summary_en: The assembly was informed of a bill authenticated by the President, the Alternative Development Finance Mobilization Bill, 2083. Subsequently, the Secretary of the National Assembly presented a message from the House of Representatives regarding the Appropriation Bill, 2083.

sections.name: Condolence Motion
sections.summary_en: A motion of condolence was presented on the passing of Rajendra Kharel, former member of the House of Representatives and former minister. The assembly observed a moment of silence in his memory and expressed condolences to his family.

sections.name: Adjournment
sections.summary_en: The meeting was adjourned until Monday, Ashad 15, 2083, at 12:15 PM.
